analysis: The open tells one story: the AI-capex bid is carrying Q4's first session while the 10Y sits at a 24-year high. Alphabet's Gemini 4 Argon (+2% at the bell) is now the confirmed catalyst, and the front-page HN thread (994 comments, 1500 points) shows the dev crowd focused on the price-war angle (one-fifth of GPT-6 Astra rates) and Artificial Analysis' verdict that Google is back among the top-three labs — pricing, not just intelligence, is the competitive weapon. Tesla split its news: the Roadster reveal was pushed to Oct 15 on weather (confirmed by two outlets), leaving tomorrow's Q3 deliveries (FactSet ~463K, down ~7% YoY) as the only near-term Tesla catalyst, and UBS's own analyst downplayed delivery significance. Nvidia's dividend-plus-$235B-buyback is shareholder-return support rather than a growth signal. The caution leg: Bespoke's breadth data (S&P constituents above 50/200-DMAs at correction-like lows) and Gundlach's 'hollow tree' warning frame the same narrow-leadership problem the indexes have to resolve. What changed vs the 6am brief: the Roadster postponement is new, JPM cut its Tesla PT to $415 with the Monday note, September's ISM print is landing right at this brief's window (GS 54.6/consensus 55.0 per zerohedge), and Brent re-tested $100 on the US-Iran stall. Signal vs noise: the 10Y level (~5.32%) and Friday's NFP are the signal; the Oracle/Tencent chip-lease report and one-off breadth warnings are worth watching, not trading.

headlines.headline: Indexes opened higher to start Q4 and October: Nasdaq +0.3%, S&P 500 +0.2%, Dow fractionally higher, with SPY and QQQ up ~0.3-0.5%. The 10Y sits around 5.32%, just below the fresh 24-year high of ~5.35% touched earlier this morning; WTI ~$91.20, Brent re-touched $100.15, bitcoin ~$83,700-83,900.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI-capex bid is overpowering the highest long-end yields since 2002 in the early session — the tape's framing is growth-vs-rates, and the 10Y's line at ~5.35% is the number to watch.

headlines.headline: Alphabet (GOOGL) +2% at the bell after last night's Gemini 4 Argon reveal: initial access to cybersecurity defenders via the Fairwind program; pricing $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, about one-fifth of GPT-6 Astra's rates. Meta +1%; the Mag-7 ETF (MAGS) +~0.5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: A concrete frontier release plus an aggressive API price war answers the DeepMind-is-lagging worry — fresh fuel for the AI-capex bid, confirmed by both Barron's and Investopedia.

headlines.headline: Tesla postponed tonight's Roadster reveal to October 15, citing severe weather for the outdoor demo near Waco. Tesla said in an X post on Monday that the event 'can only be held outdoors' — multiple outlets now carry the Oct 15 date.
headlines.why_it_matters: Removes tonight's headline catalyst — tomorrow's Q3 delivery report is now the only near-term Tesla datapoint, and the event's history of delays (8+ since 2017) keeps credibility the real question.

headlines.headline: JPMorgan cut Tesla's price target from $445 to $415 (neutral rating), trimming its Q3 delivery forecast from 516K to 482K in the same Monday note. FactSet consensus sits at ~463K, down ~7% vs Q3 2025; UBS expects ~470K. UBS's Joseph Spak downplayed deliveries' importance: 'investors increasingly are not focused on the traditional auto business.' Tesla reports deliveries tomorrow (Fri Oct 2).
headlines.why_it_matters: Two Wall Street views agree deliveries are declining year-over-year, but UBS's framing says the stock trades on the robotaxi/AI narrative instead — tomorrow's number matters mainly if it surprises far off ~463-470K.

headlines.headline: Nvidia pays its $0.25 quarterly dividend today (second straight quarter at that level, up from $0.01), and the board's Sep 28 $150B buyback add lifted remaining authorization to $235B, to be executed through fiscal 2028. Earnings context: Q2 FY27 revenue $96.2B (+106% y/y), GAAP EPS $2.46, Q3 guided $108B.
headlines.why_it_matters: Shareholder-return support (dividend + the largest buyback increase in company history) cushions the stock through the AI-capex rotation, though it's capital return, not new growth news.

headlines.headline: Micron fell in early trading on sell-the-beat despite the blowout fiscal Q4 (adj. EPS $33.42 vs $31.72 expected, revenue $54.2B vs $51.3B, guided Q1 above consensus). Memory peers Sandisk, SK Hynix, and Seagate were slightly higher ahead of the open.
headlines.why_it_matters: Textbook sell-the-news after the stock nearly quadrupled — the memory-demand story lives in the guide and the $32B in customer cash commitments, not the headline beat.

headlines.headline: Breadth caution: Bespoke data shows the share of S&P 500 stocks above their 50- and 200-day moving averages has plunged to levels normally seen in corrections, even with the cap-weighted index holding; Goldman reckons breadth is the narrowest since 2000. Jeffrey Gundlach warned the market is 'a hollow tree that could be about to snap.'
headlines.why_it_matters: The divergence the open has to resolve: a handful of AI names carry the indexes while most stocks lag — a setup where any AI-capex wobble transmits fast to the broad index.

headlines.headline: JPMorgan equity strategy (Mislav Matejka) says the Mag-7's 12-month forward P/E relative to the broader market has fallen to ~1 SD below its historical median — a 10-year low — and the de-rating has 'largely finished resetting.'
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source, unconfirmed — treat as fragile. If it holds, it reframes the AI trade as valuation-reset rather than still-derating; JPMorgan argues hyperscaler earnings strength should keep supporting the names.
